By LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:01 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 12:03 EST, 18 November 2026.

European clubs are on red alert over the futures of Liverpool stars Virgil van Dijk and Alisson – despite both players being keen to extend their contracts at Anfield.

According to recent reports, one source told me this week that AC Milan and other Italian clubs have been sniffing around Van Dijk for some time, with talks ongoing internally at those sides. Milan owner Gerry Cardinale and influential adviser Zlatan Ibrahimovic are mentioned to be huge admirers of Van Dijk, who turns 36 next summer.

Italy was also a potential destination for Alisson last summer after Juventus held talks with his camp. At one point, Juve fancied their chances of signing him.

Both players will, as it stands, be able to negotiate a free transfer to overseas clubs from January 1, but both Alisson, 34, and Van Dijk, 35, want to stay at Anfield.

It puts the ball in the court of Julian Ward, Liverpool's sporting director, who must decide what to do next.

There had been a long-standing unwritten rule at owners Fenway Sports Group of never extending deals for those over the age of 30, but this was broken in the exceptional cases of Van Dijk and Mohamed Salah 18 months ago, after the pair led Liverpool to their 20th league title.

Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson is keen to stay at the club despite reported interest from his native Brazil.

Reds captain Virgil van Dijk (right) also wants to extend his contract at Liverpool – even though AC Milan are showing interest.

Despite both players wanting to stay on Merseyside, there is understandably a great deal of interest from around the world in taking them on, with local reports linking several Brazilian clubs to Alisson recently.

In a recent development, van Dijk is a regular at Liverpool youth-team matches, which demonstrates his love of the club but may also lead to suggestions the Dutchman will move into youth coaching when he does hang up his boots. He took the first-team squad to the Liverpool FC Museum recently to learn more about the club's history – further highlighting his passion for the Reds.

Interest from abroad only strengthens the hands of Alisson and Van Dijk, however, when it comes to their demands over the salary and duration of their upcoming deals.

It has been revealed that alexis Mac Allister is another with an uncertain future, though his father and agent Carlos is hoping to hold talks with Liverpool in the coming weeks. The Argentine's future is less of a pressing issue for the Reds, though, given his deal runs until summer 2028.

Joe Gomez and Kostas Tsimikas are among the other players whose contracts are up in June next year.

It has been revealed that it was around this time last year that the wheels started to fall off the Arne Slot machine. The Dutchman was eventually sacked and we have not heard much from him since. One question I am often asked is what is Slot up to – and why has he fallen off the face of the earth?

It has been revealed that well, I can reveal the former Reds boss is biding his time and enjoying holidays with loved ones, including several trips to Ibiza. Slot and his son Joep have also visited South America, taking in games in Argentina and Brazil.

Slot, who has also been attending matches at home, turned down the Netherlands national team job and a lucrative gig in Saudi Arabia. He also rejected approaches in the summer from clubs including AC Milan, who eventually plumped for former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim.

He is waiting for the right opportunity and does not believe his stock has fallen in the same way, for example, as several axed United or Chelsea bosses. After all, Slot won the Premier League title and would be a fine hire for most clubs around Europe.

Former Liverpool boss Arne Slot (centre, bottom row) watches the Dutch Eredivisie match between Heerenveen and his old club Feyenoord earlier this month.

Slot is waiting for the right job to come up – emboldened by the knowledge he is a Premier League winner.

…but AI report makes grim reading for Arne.

A couple of interesting bits to pick out from the fantastic Global State of Football report by PLAIER, a firm spearheading the use of artificial intelligence in football.

Liverpool finished bottom of the table last season in PLAIER’s ranking of every team's coaches based on resources and how they performed – Regis Le Bris at Sunderland was top.

The Reds were in the bottom three for coaching efficiency, suggesting that squad quality alone is no guarantee of success. For a more in-depth look at the report, click here.

Reds hunt for academy recruitment guru.

Liverpool are in the process of hiring an academy ‘talent ID lead’ to help with their youth recruitment.

Sources indicate that regular readers of this column will know this area is a key metric Anfield chiefs measure success by. They are now hiring someone responsible for leading the identification and recruitment of academy talent between the ages of 13 and 18 across the UK and Ireland.

Notable recent arrivals from other academies at this age include current first-teamers Rio Ngumoha, Conor Bradley, Trey Nyoni and James McConnell.

Kop Kids: Amazing Abe lights up England duty.

In a recent development, confidential readers will recall I revealed on October 15 that Joshua Abe was ahead of schedule in his recovery from a shoulder injury and set for just another month on the sidelines. And Abe was indeed on the pitch representing England Under 17s exactly a month later, scoring against Montenegro and then again against Poland on Saturday.

In a recent development, in the last 12 months, the 16-year-old has 14 goals and four assists in just over 1,200 minutes played. Those are phenomenal numbers and it would not be a surprise to see the winger back in the first-team training group again soon.

Joshua Abe has recovered from a shoulder injury and was back in action for England Under 17s this week.

Fancy running the line, Andoni?

In the last break, the boss was spotted at the women’s Merseyside Derby. Now, he has been pictured at a local Sunday League match, taking pictures with youngsters who could not believe their luck.

These may seem like small gestures but they are a helpful way of winning hearts and minds among a fanbase whose pleas for Slot to take an active interest in all aspects of the club sometimes fell on deaf ears.

Manchester United are in town on Sunday, in case you needed reminding.

Since winning the Premier League title last year, Liverpool’s league record against the 'Big Six' is played 12, won two, drawn three, lost seven. That must improve, starting on Sunday, and there can be no excuses around a fresh-manager bounce for Mauricio Pochettino - who will barely have had time to find his parking space at Carrington by the time he comes to Anfield.

It has been revealed that liverpool need to see more from their massive-money signings Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz, who have been excellent for most of the season but poor in some high-profile fixtures, such as the home defeats by Manchester City and Arsenal. Across his 19 games against Liverpool, Pochettino has only won three matches, drawing five and losing 11.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Nolan | 19 Nov 2026 13:23.

The next instalment of the Borussen derby takes place at Borussia Park when Borussia Dortmund travel to face Borussia Monchengladbach in the Bundesliga on Saturday.

Dortmund come into the clash in second place with 21 points, trailing league-leaders Bayern Munich due to goal difference, whereas the hosts are last in 18th place with just four points.

Gladbach's situation is precarious but not irrecoverable, with the club's tally of four points five fewer than 15th-placed FC Koln, who are the first team outside of the relegation zone.

Head coach Alexander Blessin has only overseen six games as boss, winning twice and losing on three occasions, but his team have taken four points from the last nine on offer in the Bundesliga.

Their latest result was a 3-1 loss against Hamburger SV on November 6, though they did win two and drawn one of their prior three fixtures.

Die Fohlen may ranks as the division's worst defensive team having conceded 25 goals in nine games, but their return of 12 goals in the final third is the second best total in the bottom six.

While Gladbach were defeated in their first three home matches of 2026-27, they have since won once and settled for a stalemate once at Borussia Park, though they are still winless at the ground in the league this season (W0, D1, L3).

Dortmund could find themselves trailing Bayern by three points by the time they face Gladbach due to the fact the Bavarians play against FC Koln on Friday.

Niko Kovac will be delighted by his side's start to the campaign considering 21 points is their joint best tally after nine matchweeks in 13 seasons.

BVB's most recent result was a 2-1 success against Elversberg on November 7, and that was their fifth triumph in six contests.

The club scored at least two goals in five of those fixtures, and though they only managed to keep one clean sheet in that time, no club has conceded fewer goals in the Bundesliga (seven).

Black and Yellow were beaten 1-0 in the corresponding meeting in 2025-26, losing 1-0 at Borussia Park in May, but they emerged victorious in five of their previous six encounters with Gladbach.

Dortmund have taken eight points from a possible 12 on the road in the Bundesliga this term, while they have lost one, drawn two and won just one of their last four outings away from home in all competitions.

Gladbach will have to contend with numerous absences, including suspended centre-back Ko Itakura and injured striker Tim Kleindienst.

Expect to see Kevin Diks, Philipp Sander and Fabio Chiarodia in the backline, while Isac Lidberg may be trusted to lead the line up front.

As for Dortmund, there are still doubts about the availability of centre-forward Serhou Guirassy, who could have to settle for a place on the bench in favour of Fabio Silva.

Jobe Bellingham and Felix Nmecha have often featured together, and they are the most likely duo to start together in a double pivot.

Emre Can is closing in on a return from a cruciate ligament injury, but he is not ready to play on Saturday, so perhaps fans will see a three-man defence consisting of Joane Gadou, Waldemar Anton and Nico Schlotterbeck.

Borussia Monchengladbach possible starting lineup:.

Nicolas; Diks, Sander, Chiarodia; Scally, Uno, Neuhaus, Castrop; Bolin, Lidberg, Mohya.

Borussia Dortmund possible starting lineup:.

Kobel; Gadou, Anton, Schlotterbeck; Beier, Bellingham, Nmecha, Svensson; Karetsas, Sabitzer; Silva.

It is difficult to look past Gladbach's poor defensive record given they are the most porous team in the division.

Even if Dortmund fail to keep a clean sheet, there is little evidence to suggest they will suffer a collapse at the back and drop points at Borussia Park.

By Carter White | 19 Nov 2026 13:37, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 13:38.

Real Madrid have revealed that Aurelien Tchouameni has signed a contraction extension until June 2032.

The 26-year-old and Jose Mourinho's men have made a decent start to the 2026-27 campaign, with Los Blancos sitting second place in the La Liga standings, just three points behind arch rivals Barcelona.

Following the final international break of the calendar year, Real Madrid return to action at the Bernabeu on Saturday afternoon, when top-flight regulars Celta Vigo are the visitors in La Liga.

The makeup of Los Blancos' squad has shifted massively over the past few years as a number of fresh attacking stars have arrived, including French superstar Kylian Mbappe and England's Jude Bellingham.

With his influence waning, Vinicius Junior has endured a difficult start to the current campaign, with the Brazil international struggling since Real Madrid waved goodbye to German legend Toni Kroos.

Communicating to supporters worldwide on their official website, Real Madrid confirmed some exciting news involving Tchouameni, who has started seven La Liga matches so far in the 2026-27 term.

Los Blancos have declared that the 26-year-old has put pen to paper on a bumper contract extension at the Bernabeu, committing his long-term future to the 15-time European champions.

Tchouameni's deal with Real Madrid now expires in June 2032, meaning that the Frenchman could spend a decade at the Spanish giants if he sees out at the length of his recently-agreed terms.

The midfielder joined from Ligue 1 outfit Monaco in the summer of 2022 on a deal running until June 2028, meaning that he was approaching the conclusion of his initial agreement at the club.

Tchouameni started the La Liga victories over Barcelona (2-1), Racing Santander (3-0) and Valencia (3-0) prior to the November international break and should play once again versus Celta Vigo on Saturday.

Racking up over 200 competitive appearances since his 2022 arrival from France, Tchouameni has become part of the furniture at Real Madrid, who are looking to repeat their former glories.

The departure of legendary German Kroos left a massive hole to fill in the middle of the park, and Los Blancos are focused on bringing through the next generation of club heroes under head coach Mourinho.

Tchouameni featured in a staggering 55 matches across all competitions for Real Madrid last season, highlighting his importance to a side who have their work cut out chasing down Barcelona this term.

Cambio nel Napoli: esce Melynk ed entra Liccardo.

44′ Barido prova a sorprendere Strappini con una punizione beffarda, l’estremo difensore riesce a rientrare e a far suo il pallone.

42′ Favicchio premia la progressione di Santella sulla sinistra, traversone al centro bloccato da Strappini.

36′ Conclusione dalla distanza di sinistro da parre di Melnyk: sfera che si spegne sul fondo.

31′ Ammonito Malfatti per un brutto fallo su Zappalà.

In a recent development, 28′ Grande occasione per il Perugia! Palla dalla sinistra raccolta da Vanni in piena area di rigore partenopea, che controlla e conclude di sinistro: pallone a lato.

27′ Il Napoli reclama un rigore per una trattenuta (non pesantissima, ma c’è), di Di Salvatore su Melnyk: l’arbitro ha fatto continuare.

It has been revealed that 23′ Occasione Napoli! Favicchio serve sulla corsia sinistra Baridò, che conclude in porta: Cesarini devia. L’azzurrino poteva sia servire Esposito che concludere in maniera più incisiva.

Recent findings suggest that 19′ Calcio di punizione di Perugini respinto dalla barriera, pallone che, per poco, non diventa buono l’inserimento sul secondo palo di Pierangelini. Corner per gli ospiti.

18′ Ammonito Vanni per un brutto fallo su Chiummariello, partito in ripartenza.

In a recent development, 17′ Doppia grande occasione per il Perugia! Corner corto di Di Salvatore: traversone che pesca Merci, il cui tiro viene deviato e sfiora l’incrocio dei pali. Sull’angolo successivo stacca Peruzzi, ma è bravissimo Saviano a deviare nei pressi della linea di porta.

11′ GOOL NAPOLI! Ottima sponda di Saviano per Favicchio, che si accentra e beffa Strappini con una conclusione di destro che si insacca nell’angolino.

9′ Imbucata per Cianni, che prova a mettere il pallone in mezzo: bravissimo Merone a leggere la giocata e a bloccare in uscita il pallone.

Industry observers note that 6′ Perugia pericoloso! Cross al centro per Pierangelini che, in area di rigore partenopea, colpisce il pallone con la spalla e non di testa: sfera che si spegne sul fondo.

3′ Santella si propone sulla sinistra e realizza un traversone al centro che, però, viene bloccato da Strappini.

Benvenuti alla diretta testuale di IamNaples.it di Napoli-Perugia, gara valida per la nona giornata del campionato Primavera 2 girone B. Gli azzurrini sono decimi, a cinque punti dalla zona play-off, proprio il Bari occupa l’ultima posizione utile per andare oltre la regular season. Il primo posto vale la promozione diretta, in questo momento lo occupa il Catanzaro che ha dieci punti in più degli azzurrini. A Cercola arriva il Perugia che è terzo in classifica con diciotto punti, otto in più del Napoli. La squadra di Nocerino in campionato è reduce da due pareggi a reti bianche contro Monopoli e Frosinone mentre il Perugia, dopo la sconfitta di Benevento, prima della sosta ha battuto 3-2 il Pescara.

It has been revealed that davide Nicola è solo l'ultimo degli allenatori che hanno parlato dell'uscita di GTA VI in conferenza stampa. Il tecnico del Venezia ha risposto così a chi gli chiedeva se qualche suo giocatore avesse chiesto un permesso speciale per usufruirne: "Sarei più preoccupato se si preoccupassero dei giochi, alla loro età mi dedicavo ad altro... Ma nella loro vita privata possono fare ciò che vogliono, l'importante è fare tutto con buon senso e giusto peso. Poi se qualcuno rimanesse chiuso per giorni a giocare per giorni beh, mi dispiacerebbe per lui, ci sono tante altre cose da fare".

Industry observers note that in cosa dovete ancora migliorare? "Interpretare una fase non basta, bisogna interpretare una fase e la sua transizione. Se sei efficace in attacco crei già i presupposti per una fase difensiva, e viceversa. Stiamo progredendo sui concetti in maniera brillanti per alcuni, per altri dobbiamo migliorare e assimilarli".

L’ex presidente e allenatore vede buone prospettive, ma ricorda che la squadra è ancora all’inizio del cammino.

Dino Zoff considera meritato il primo posto della Lazio e guarda con fiducia alle prospettive della squadra. L’ex portiere, già presidente e allenatore biancoceleste, ha parlato anche di Mandas e della Nazionale.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 19 Nov 2026 14:04.

Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has reportedly prepared to enter talks over the Old Trafford future of Bruno Fernandes.

The 54-year-old Argentine arrives at the Theatre of Dreams with the Red Devils sitting 18th in the Premier League table after winning just one of their opening 10 top-flight games of 2026-27.

That woeful run was eventually enough to remove Michael Carrick from his post at Man Utd, with the club's hierarchy moving swiftly to lure Pochettino away from his duties with the United States on the international scene.

As well as Carrick, wonderkid JJ Gabriel has also departed the Red Devils this month, with the teenage sensation set to sign for European giants Real Madrid despite failing to make a first-team appearance for United.

Looking to avoid an unthinkable relegation this season, Man Utd are plotting significant additions to the playing squad during the January transfer window, with a Greek striker supposedly catching the eye.

According to transfer specialist Fabrizio Romano via Football Transfers, new Manchester United head coach Pochettino is set to be immediately involved in major talks at the Theatre of Dreams.

The report states that the Red Devils and captain Fernandes have been locked in discussions over a contract extension for the past five months, with an agreement yet to be reached by the two parties.

The 32-year-old's current deal at Old Trafford expires in June 2027, meaning that the Portuguese playmaker would be able to depart on a free transfer at the conclusion of this season.

It is understood that Man Utd are aiming to avoid that scenario, and now incoming boss Pochettino is set to join talks with the player and the club over the future of the influential attacker.

Fernandes supposedly retains interest from clubs in Italy, Saudi Arabia and Turkey, with Champions League-competing Galatasaray attempting to bring the former Sporting Lisbon man to Istanbul over the summer.

Whilst Manchester United's transfer activity since the exit of Sir Alex Ferguson has come under deserved criticism, there is no doubt that the signing of Fernandes was an excellent move by the fallen English powerhouses.

The 32-year-old has been an almost ever-present in the Red Devils ranks since joining from the Primeira Liga in January 2020, scoring 113 goals across a total of 341 competitive appearances.

Fernandes broke the Premier League assist record last season despite his side's immense struggles, and that theme of shining amid the chaos extends throughout the attacker's time in England.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Seye Omidiora | 19 Nov 2026 14:06, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 09:24.
  • Thomas Frank's first assignment as Crystal Palace boss takes him to Coventry City for Saturday's gameweek 11 encounter at the Coventry Building Society Arena.
  • The Eagles manager's immediate priority will be lifting the South London side off the bottom of the Premier League table, a position that prompted Pierre Sage's swift departure after 10 top-flight matches.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 19 Nov 2026 14:06, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 09:24.

Thomas Frank's first assignment as Crystal Palace boss takes him to Coventry City for Saturday's gameweek 11 encounter at the Coventry Building Society Arena.

The Eagles manager's immediate priority will be lifting the South London side off the bottom of the Premier League table, a position that prompted Pierre Sage's swift departure after 10 top-flight matches.

Palace have spent 14 consecutive seasons in the Premier League, and the capital club's board have taken drastic action to ensure that number becomes 15 at the end of the current campaign.

The Selhurst Park outfit entered the November international break in dire straits after a 3-1 loss to Andoni Iraola's Liverpool, marking their fourth consecutive top-flight defeat following setbacks against rivals Brighton & Hove Albion, Newcastle United and Tottenham Hotspur.

Particularly striking during that run were their struggles in front of goal and defensive frailties, highlighted by an alarming 12-1 aggregate score across those defeats that ultimately cost Sage his job.

Frank's reputation suffered during his spell as Spurs boss last season, but his previous work at Brentford should give the Selhurst Park faithful confidence that a turnaround is possible.

Nonetheless, it remains to be seen whether the Dane has conveyed his ideas in less than a week of training, with the international break also denying him access to his full squad, as the London club seek to end their four-match losing sequence.

A first victory since October and third overall would lift them above this weekend's 17th-placed hosts and potentially out of the bottom three, although the latter outcome depends on results elsewhere.

Coventry's 3-1 defeat at Everton before the pause left Frank Lampard's men alongside Arsenal and Manchester City as the only clubs yet to draw in this season's Premier League campaign.

However, while the defending champions and Man City occupy positions in the top three, Coventry's nine points leave them just one clear of the relegation places heading into a busy period.

Lampard's men can take encouragement from collecting six of those points in front of their adoring supporters, who witnessed October victories of 4-1 over Newcastle and 3-1 against Sunderland either side of a narrow 1-0 defeat to Fulham.

Although the absence of home clean sheets remains concerning, the Sky Blues' seven goals across their last three matches at the Coventry Building Society Arena represent clear progress after they failed to score in opening defeats to Hull City (1-0) and Brighton (5-0).

Now, the West Midlands side aim to secure consecutive home Premier League victories to avoid slipping into the bottom three.

Coventry City Premier League form:.

Crystal Palace Premier League form:.

Crystal Palace form (all competitions):.

Caleb Yirenkyi and Bobby Thomas (calf) are doubtful for Coventry this weekend, while Luke Woolfenden (knee) and Josh Eccles (ankle) face late fitness tests; however, Frank Onyeka, Aurele Amenda (calf), Haji Wright (thigh) and Ephron Mason-Clark (knee) are expected to miss out.

Jack Rudoni is the only home player to have scored more than once, with the attacking midfielder's three goals accounting for 30% of the Sky Blues' tally of 10 this term.

After registering assists in consecutive appearances against Newcastle and Spurs in October, Brandon Thomas-Asante has dropped to the bench, but the Ghanaian forward will hope to play a pivotal role for Lampard's team this weekend.

One Palace player denied the opportunity to make an immediate impression is Jean-Philippe Mateta, who serves the second game of a three-match suspension following his straight red card in October's 2-0 defeat at Spurs.

Further concerns surround Ismaila Sarr (groin) and Jorgen Strand Larsen (ankle), who are doubtful for this weekend's encounter and could leave Frank without several match-winners.

While former Arsenal defender Takehiro Tomiyasu (calf) is also touch-and-go for Saturday's match, Chadi Riad's knee injury will keep him sidelined until 2027.

Coventry City possible starting lineup:.

Rushworth; Van Ewijk, Mfuni, Pinnock, Dasilva; Torp, Grimes; Sakamoto, Rudoni, Gboho; Awoniyi.

Crystal Palace possible starting lineup:.

Henderson; Richards, Disasi, Lerma; Mingueza, Wharton, Timber, Mitchell; Kamada, Pino; Nketiah.

Frank's appointment should provide Palace with renewed purpose, but Mateta's suspension and doubts over Sarr and Strand Larsen leave the visitors short of attacking options.

Coventry have scored seven goals across their last three home matches and could exploit the Eagles' defensive uncertainty to spoil the Dane's first assignment.

Le parole del calciatore biancoceleste nel pre partita di Lazio-Lecce.

Poco prima del fischio d’inizio di Lazio-Lecce, il difensore biancoceleste Diogo Leite ha parlato ai microfoni di Dazn e Lazio Style Radio, soffermandosi su diverse tematiche legate al match in programma alle ore 15:00.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Sources indicate that sono sempre più in confidenza con il gioco e con quello che mi dice il mister. Mi aiuta a integrarmi e a far capire le sue indicazioni. Sto studiando l'italiano e fra qualche mese spero di parlarlo.

Sources indicate that questa partita sarà come le altre. Giochiamo a casa e vogliamo mantenere questo buon inizio di stagione. Vogliamo continuare così, stiamo andando bene.

Dobbiamo fare attenzione perché gli avversari possono essere pericolosi. Ma abbiamo preparato bene la partita. Lavoriamo sui calci piazzati sempre, possono essere importanti. Dobbiamo fare bene sia in attacco che in difesa. Doekhi? Sono contento di giocare insieme a lui. Ci conosciamo ormai da molto tempo e sappiamo come giochiamo insieme. Sono molto tranquillo in coppia con lui, vogliamo fare bene.

Thomas Tuchel faces a fight to regain the full trust of his England players, despite claiming that “99.9 per cent” of supporters do not talk about the semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Telegraph Sport reported that players were shocked and disappointed by Tuchel’s approach to the final 30 minutes of the World Cup semi-final.

It can now be revealed that doubts linger among England players over Tuchel’s ability to get the best out of his squad and ultimately lead them to glory in the next European Championship.

There is also some lasting unhappiness over Tuchel’s perceived unwillingness to take ultimate responsibility for England’s World Cup exit and his claim that ball possession was not in “the DNA” of the nation’s players.

It has been revealed that tuchel has spoken of fostering a “brotherhood” within the England squad, but a source told Telegraph Sport: “He still has work to do to get all the players fully behind him again. What happened at the World Cup and some of his comments caused some damage that has not just disappeared.”.

Tuchel has no concerns over the commitment of his players and stated: “I have no doubt how keen they are. No doubt. I know them, I was seven weeks with them. We had a qualification campaign together, we are 18 months together, I have no doubt that we step up and produce performances in the next cycle. I’m responsible for that.”.

Industry observers note that one player who did not travel to the World Cup and is not part of Tuchel’s latest England squad for four Nations League games is Morgan Gibbs-White. His partner, Britney De Villiers, took a swipe at Tuchel by posting an image on Instagram that referenced the fact the Nottingham Forest man is the only Premier League player to have created five or more chances in every match he has played this season.

There is no immediate sign that Tuchel is ready to change his approach, as he refused to accept the country were angered by his tactics and substitutions in the Argentina game.

In an attempt to gloss over the nature of England’s missed opportunity in the United States, Tuchel claimed that the bronze-medal victory over France was “one of the nicest experiences ever” for supporters and that he did not lose any sleep over his World Cup squad selection.

Tuchel’s defence of the World Cup campaign also included the revelation that his Football Association bosses had assured the England head coach that his job was safe before the last-16 victory over Mexico.

In a recent development, “I tell you something, like 99.9 per cent of the fans don’t speak about substitutions, tactical twists,” Tuchel said. “They speak about where they have watched the Mexico game, they speak about the second half, the energy of the Croatia match, they speak about how nerve-wracking it was to watch our match against Congo and where they celebrated.

“This is how it should be, this is what a World Cup is for, to connect with the people and to give them experiences that they will not forget. And this is the feedback that I get.”.

Asked if he had received any negative feedback at all since the World Cup, Tuchel answered: “No. Not at all. Do you think that’s necessary? I had some quite bad stuff between Argentina and France. [But] No [not since I’ve been back in England].”.

The FA publicly backed Tuchel after the defeat by Argentina, but the German has now revealed that he was privately told his job was safe well before that.

Even if England had lost to Mexico and failed to reach the last eight of the World Cup, Tuchel has claimed he would not have been sacked. He stated: “There was a moment, a very special moment, before the Mexico game where we had a talk and my bosses told me ‘we know that anything can happen in a football match, we know that anything can happen in a match in Mexico, in a World Cup match, but don’t worry, we see what’s going on and we want to continue like this’.

Industry observers note that “It was a beautiful moment for me as a coach. I felt this kind of freedom to take my choices and to just coach freely, and there was never a doubt in my mind that we would continue together and there was obviously never a doubt in their mind.”.

England secured their best World Cup finish since 1966 by winning the bronze-medal game against France in a chaotic match in Miami.

“If you look at the 6-4 against France, people talk about it like it’s one of their nicest experiences ever, to watch a football match,” Tuchel said. “So maybe I have to compromise in my wish for control, for a little bit more chaos, embrace the chaos, and maybe it brings out the best.”.

He has recalled Cole Palmer and Trent Alexander-Arnold to his squad, but insists he has lost no sleep over not taking the pair to the World Cup.

According to recent reports, “I was very happy with the [World Cup] squad selection, we put a lot of effort and emphasis into the squad selection,” Tuchel stated. “And I had a lot of sleepless nights, but I had not one sleepless night about our selection, because I was more than seven weeks with this group of players, and they were nothing but fantastic. I think the spirit that we built and the mentality that we revealed brought us to the place that we got.

But the question that is also still lingering around is, who knows what would have happened? Who knows if we hadn’t made any substitutions what would have happened? “So, there’s not much sense in torturing ourselves, looking back. It’s moving forward, but the team, like I noted, did brilliantly. And I will not allow 30 minutes against Argentina to override how we view this World Cup.”.

Reading will be looking for an immediate response after suffering a 3-1 defeat to fellow promotion contenders Stockport County last weekend.

Jack Marriott equalised for the Royals after Kyle Wootton had opened the scoring, but goals from Ethan Ennis and Jack Diamond ultimately earned an important victory for the Hatters.

That result saw Leam Richardson's side drop out of the playoff places, although they could return to the top six with a victory over Bromley if other results go their way.

The veteran striker has scored in his last two games across all competitions and bagged a total of nine goals in 10 league games.

Bromley, meanwhile, have struggled to make the step up to League One and are bottom of the division with just nine points from 13 games.

The Ravens are without a win in their last 10 games across all competitions and new manager Karl Robinson claims they "need to evolve" and "stick together" if they are to stay up this season.

Bromley's trip to Reading will be Robinson's first league game in charge, following a 2-0 defeat to Rotherham United in the FA Cup and a 2-1 defeat to MK Dons in the EFL Trophy.

It is worth noting that Bromley have never beaten Reading in a competitive fixture, although they did draw 1-1 in the EFL Cup earlier this season before the Royals triumphed on penalties.

"Come club abbiamo una grande responsabilità e la Fondazione è davvero importante nella nostra società perché rispecchia i nostri valori, aiuta la comunità e questo per noi conta molto. Le nostre porte sono sempre aperte per accogliere quei ragazzi. Sono importanti per noi. È davvero bello. Le nostre porte, Milanello, sono il loro Milanello, quindi ne sono davvero felice. Rispecchia il nostro modo di affrontare la vita. Sono molto importanti per noi e li vogliamo più vicini: sarà una bella partita per loro, una gara divertente contro un'ottima squadra, quindi sarà un bel match da vedere".

Alcuni giocatori non sono disponibili, ma sono davvero soddisfatto di chi sta giocando perché è il modo migliore per mantenere il ritmo, quindi siamo pronti per la partita”.

Che tipo di squadra è il Frosinone? "Per me è divertente guardare il loro ritmo: sono la squadra che fa più scatti, e il loro passo è davvero alto. Noi siamo i migliori negli scatti, quindi penso che siamo in grado di reggere il confronto. Sono molto bravi nell'uno contro uno sulle fasce. Guardando molte partite del Frosinone, è difficile capire i loro movimenti perché c'è una sorta di logica nel caos che creano, ma è complicato da decifrare. Rispetto a noi, sono nettamente più bravi a portare il pallone nell'ultimo terzo di campo. So che giocano con uno stile diverso: è più diretto, soprattutto quando recuperano palla, e questo permette loro di avere più possessi nella trequarti offensiva. Non impiegano molto tempo a preparare le giocate, quindi per noi sarà fondamentale, quando abbiamo la palla, pensare già a cosa fare se la perdiamo. Sarà una partita davvero difficile e, come ho detto contro il Venezia, ci sono alcune squadre contro cui dobbiamo restare molto concentrati perché so che quello stile di gioco può creare parecchi problemi. Mi aspetto quindi una gara molto complessa, ma abbiamo anche noi la nostra idea per mettere in difficoltà l'avversario.”.

Serve una mano a Ramos? Anche dal mercato? "Sono due domande diverse. Certo, possiamo dire che magari un'opzione in più potrebbe essere una buona cosa per aiutare Camarda e Ramos, ma penso che le difficoltà di Ramos siano le difficoltà della squadra. Ho avuto due settimane per capire i dati che avete voi e che ho io. Non stiamo raggiungendo l'ultimo terzo di campo. Siamo una delle peggiori squadre nell'entrare nell'ultimo terzo e restarci. Quindi non abbiamo molti tiri. Non voglio una squadra che faccia tanti tiri da fuori area perché la maggior parte delle volte non si segna da fuori area. Ma non stiamo aiutando Ramos. Non stiamo aiutando Cisse. Cisse ha molti gol, ma in una posizione diversa. Arriva in area e quello che vedo contro il Genoa è che senza Ramos non segniamo quei due gol. Non ha segnato, ma senza Ramos non segniamo quei due gol. Ma la mia preoccupazione più grande è la squadra ed è la quantità di volte, è il volume nella fase offensiva. Non possiamo continuare così perché stiamo segnando con questo volume molti gol, ma se pensate che possiamo mantenere questo ritmo con meno volume e più gol, non accadrà. Non saremo in grado di continuare così. Quindi il mio obiettivo è spingere la squadra in avanti. Questo è il mio lavoro, non il lavoro di Ramos, e dobbiamo spingere tutti i nostri giocatori, Ramos, Camarda, Pulisic, Rabiot, tutti questi ragazzi vicino all'area. Quindi Ramos è in difficoltà perché la squadra è in difficoltà, ma Ramos è quello che segue di più il centrocampista, il difensore centrale. So che non è il suo compito. So che abbiamo comprato un giocatore per fare gol, ma non stiamo facendo, non sto facendo il mio lavoro per aiutare Ramos, mentre Ramos sta facendo di tutto per aiutare me. E so che Ramos segnerà molti gol, ma dobbiamo spingere la squadra in avanti affinché possa giocare nella posizione di centravanti. Quindi la mia sensazione sull'ultima partita è che senza Ramos, senza quel movimento e senza dire di passare a Cisse, non c'è gol. Ha recuperato palla, ha fatto l'assist per Pulisic. Senza Ramos non c'è gol. Quindi il mio obiettivo è vincere le partite e non importa chi segna, ma devo essere giusto con i miei giocatori. Devo fare il mio lavoro e spingere la squadra in avanti per avere più volume in attacco.”.

Sources indicate that 24 punti in 11 giornate: sei soddisfatto? "Difficile dirlo. Immaginate se giochiamo come contro la Juventus: sarei davvero soddisfatto con 24 punti. Se guardate la nostra partita contro l'Inter, sarei davvero frustrato perché abbiamo solo 24 punti. Quindi non ragiono in questo modo. Penso che stiamo crescendo come squadra abbastanza velocemente e cambiamo il modo in cui giochiamo abbastanza velocemente, ma non sono soddisfatto del momento della squadra. E, come vi ho detto, non solo nella fase offensiva: il volume di una grande squadra deve essere molto migliore. Quindi penso di non essere soddisfatto della posizione in campionato. Non sono contento delle nostre prestazioni, ma devo anche dire che sono davvero soddisfatto del modo in cui i giocatori stanno comprendendo il nostro modo di giocare. E poi, ovviamente, mi farete quella domanda magari nei prossimi giorni sull'Europa. Dobbiamo fare meglio in Europa. Quindi sono felice di essere qui. Penso che stiamo crescendo molto velocemente come squadra, ma non sono sempre contento delle prestazioni. Questo è sicuro".

Sources indicate that come aiutare Ramos? "Penso che dipenda dagli avversari, dipende dal momento della squadra. Non credo che se giochi con più attaccanti o punte, allora raggiungerai di più l'ultimo terzo di campo. A volte succede con più centrocampisti, a volte con un diverso tipo di difensori centrali. Le caratteristiche dei giocatori possono aiutarci, ma dobbiamo anche adattarci a questo quando affrontiamo avversari diversi. Quindi non so cosa accadrà, ma in alcune partite cambieremo le caratteristiche".

Industry observers note that cosa pensate di fare con Camarda? "Anche io ero un giocatore giovane che voleva tutto molto velocemente, e penso che questo succeda con un ragazzo che ha davvero tanta voglia di giocare, il che è una buona cosa. Mi piace molto. Credo abbia bisogno di tempo per adattarsi a un livello diverso. Giocare per il Milan è davvero difficile. È difficile per un ragazzo che ha esperienza come Ramos, di cui parlavate prima, figuriamoci per Camarda. Quindi ha bisogno di tempo per crescere, per sentirsi ambientato nel club. Non so cosa succederà a gennaio. Deve restare concentrato su queste partite. Nel calcio tutto cambia in una settimana, figuriamoci da qui a gennaio. Quindi l'obiettivo è il prossimo allenamento, la prossima partita, e può succedere di tutto. Sono davvero soddisfatto di come è tornato, forse perché ha cambiato ambiente. Ho sentito che Baldini ha parlato con lui. Non so cosa abbia detto al ragazzo, ma è tornato più felice. Quindi sono davvero contento per questa chiacchierata con Baldini e sono molto felice per Camarda. Queste cose possono succedere ai ragazzi giovani in un grande club: deve solo concentrarsi sul prossimo allenamento, godersi la prossima partita e le cose andranno a posto. Capisco la domanda su gennaio, ma gennaio è ancora molto lontano. Concentriamoci sulla prossima partita".

According to recent reports, ha capito perché la squadra cala dopo il vantaggio? "Abbiamo tutte le informazioni su questo aspetto, e a volte vado anche oltre: talvolta, quando siamo in vantaggio, abbassiamo il livello in ogni azione della partita, quindi è qualcosa su cui stiamo lavorando. Penso che stiamo gestendo meglio le partite. Se guardate la partita contro il Genoa, abbiamo controllato meglio il secondo tempo senza creare moltissimo pericolo, ma stiamo gestendo meglio quei momenti. Se confrontate Atalanta con Inter, e anche con il Genoa, stiamo migliorando su questo piano, ma resta un aspetto da correggere. Credo però che sia collegato al volume di gioco. Se non creiamo pericolo, se non minacciamo abbastanza l'avversario quando siamo in vantaggio, possiamo andare un po' in difficoltà. Quindi dobbiamo spingere la squadra in avanti con il pallone. Non è solo controllare il gioco, ma anche creare le occasioni per chiudere le partite. Perciò dobbiamo senz'altro intervenire su questo e ci stiamo già riflettendo”.

Industry observers note that C'è l'esigenza un nuovo terzino sinistro? "Quella col Genoa con Musah era una situazione specifica. Non lo so e non vi dirò cosa stiamo pensando per gennaio. Ma quella partita, per esempio, riguardava il piano fisico. Avevamo giocato tante gare. Era una questione di fisicità. Volevo il piede destro per via di tutte le corse, e avete visto gli inserimenti di Adrien Rabiot; il piede destro perché era uomo contro uomo, e dare palla di prima era un dettaglio semplice che poteva aiutarci a mantenere il possesso. Musah è molto forte in questo. È un centrocampista in più per avere il possesso del pallone. Musah non giocherà terzino sinistro domani, ve lo posso assicurare. Però è un'opzione. È un'opzione, e sono davvero contento di avere giocatori che credo siano il futuro del calcio, cioè avere elementi che possono ricoprire posizioni diverse. Quindi non so cosa succederà a gennaio, ma abbiamo giocatori in grado di fare quel ruolo. A volte, però, bisogna solo adattarsi all'avversario, al momento, al contesto”.

Industry observers note that come ha trovato Pulisic? "Il rinnovo penso che aiuti qualsiasi giocatore sentire la fiducia del club, ed è stato chiaro che la società gli ha mostrato il rinnovo di contratto, e questo aiuta sempre un calciatore. Poi vi avevo detto, quando non giocava, che Pulisic è davvero importante per noi, ma non possiamo dimenticare gli infortuni, il modo in cui dobbiamo gestire il giocatore in base al contesto. Oggi posso dirvi che Pulisic è forse il giocatore che non possiamo sostituire. Per la capacità di girarsi tra le linee non abbiamo un altro Pulisic, e ci sono stati alcuni momenti in Europa, in quest'ultimo ciclo di partite, in cui abbiamo dovuto preservarlo un po'. Quindi non c'è niente di meglio che dire che Pulisic ha delle caratteristiche tali per cui, se non lo abbiamo in campo, la squadra sente molto la sua assenza. Da questo potete capire quanto sia fondamentale per noi. Non è il tipo di ragazzo che parla molto, ma parla sul campo senza bisogno di parole. Vuole sempre il pallone e lo si è percepito contro il Genoa. Se guardate tutte le giocate, Pulisic è quello che trascina la squadra, lui e Rabiot, e penso che questi due giocatori siano a un livello tale per cui, se ci manca uno di loro, siamo in difficoltà. Non mi piace parlare dei singoli, ma devo farlo. Penso che tutti possano capirlo. Quindi Pulisic è il nostro presente, sarà il nostro futuro e credo abbia il potenziale per fare ancora di più.”.

Il mercato di gennaio vi aiuterà? "Molti club fanno un errore del genere. Molti grandi club ragionano guardando la classifica: se siamo vicini, facciamo investimenti folli; se non siamo vicini, non investiamo. Credo che il punto chiave sia avere un piano a lungo termine. Se perdi tutte le partite ed esoneri l'allenatore, è normale, non parlo di questo. Quello che dico è di restare fedeli al proprio piano. Noi abbiamo un piano. Che tipo di giocatore vogliamo? Uno in grado di fare tutte le corse che chiediamo, con il carattere che cerchiamo. Non una grande stella, ma un ragazzo equilibrato, che arrivi qui per essere parte integrante della squadra. Se abbiamo le idee ben chiare e andiamo a prendere il meglio possibile - giovane o esperto, meglio giovane in questo momento - ma con un piano preciso, non bisogna guardare la classifica. La classifica va guardata per valutare il percorso, ma per comprare, per investire per i prossimi cinque anni, non si guarda la classifica. Credo che questo sia l'errore più grande dei club: provare a vincere il titolo spendendo tutto e subito, cercando di diventare campioni a suon di soldi. È lo sbaglio più grande. Noi abbiamo quindi un piano chiaro. Non conta la classifica: andremo a prendere ciò che vogliamo in modo molto netto, e questo non cambierà. Guardando la classifica e guardando i nostri giocatori, possiamo fare meglio. Possiamo vincere contro il Ferencvaros, che è un'ottima squadra? Possiamo giocare meglio contro quell'avversario? Con i nostri giocatori possiamo farlo. Abbiamo un percorso ben definito e non cambieremo ciò che vogliamo solo perché guardiamo la classifica a dicembre o a gennaio. Abbiamo un piano chiaro su cosa fare.”.

Ha messo regole per GTA6? “Lascio rispondere al mio amico mister Gennaro Gattuso. No, ragazzi, non mi interessa. Devono essere pronti. Se non sono pronti, un altro prenderà il loro posto. Non importa chi sia, quindi non sono preoccupato. Credo che non sappia nemmeno Luka Modric cosa sia. Quindi, mister Gattuso, penso abbia detto tutto.”.

È un sognatore che non si arrende? “L'obiettivo è vincere ogni partita. Se guardate il mio percorso, tutti i club che ho scelto, è chiaro che sono un sognatore. Sono semplicemente felice di essere qui e voglio davvero far parte di questa società, magari per il resto della mia carriera, perché voglio mettermi radici. È un club da sogno, ma so che devo dimostrarlo contro il Frosinone. In caso contrario... Siete stati davvero gentili con me, anche molto gentili in questa settimana. Grazie mille, ragazzi. Conosco l'altra faccia della medaglia, quindi dobbiamo vincere perché, altrimenti, mi aspetto un approccio diverso da parte vostra. Quindi sono un sognatore, ma sono molto concentrato sul lavoro e penso che possiamo vincere ogni partita fino alla fine di dicembre. Non sogno altro. Se voglio chiedere qualcosa, tipo il rientro di Saelemaekers molto veloce, quello Chukwueze molto veloce...".

By Carter White | 19 Nov 2026 14:43.

Barcelona have reportedly earmarked Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez and two other defenders as transfer targets ahead of the January window.

Hansi Flick's men have enjoyed an excellent start to the 2026-27 campaign on the domestic scene, winning 11 of their opening 12 top-flight contests, meaning that they sit top of the La Liga standings.

Barca have been linked heavily to new defensive additions in recent times, including Tottenham Hotspur man Pedro Perro, however, it is believed that the Catalans are not pursuing a deal for the World Cup winner in the New Year.

Head coach Flick is supposedly targeting the signing of a centre-back and a full-back during the upcoming trading point, aiming to strengthen his side's chances of winning the Champions League for the first time since 2015.

Hoping to record four consecutive competitive victories, Barcelona welcome Europe-chasing Villarreal to Camp Nou on Sunday afternoon, when club action will return following the international break.

As per Spanish publication Mundo Deportivo, Barcelona will press forward in their search for a new defender during the January transfer window, in which head coach Flick is expected to be backed by sporting director Deco.

The report claims that Barca are keen on the cost-effective option of bringing Manchester United centre-back Martinez to the club, with the 2022 World Cup winner approaching the end of his contract at Old Trafford.

As well as the outspoken United star, it is understood that the La Liga leaders are also eyeing up a move for Borussia Dortmund's Nico Schlotterbeck, who is capable of playing at centre-back and left-back.

The 26-year-old was given his senior Germany debut by Barca boss Flick in March 2022, and the Dortmund sweetheart is supposedly available for £50m ahead of the winter transfer window.

Finally, it is believed that Barca's hierarchy are yet to shelve the possibility of signing Inter Milan and Italy defender Alessandro Bastoni, who is said to be open to a La Liga switch amid a £33m valuation.

After his explosive comments following defeat by Atletico Madrid in the Champions League, Martinez created a major rift between himself and the Manchester United board, as well as former head coach Carrick.

The general consensus is that the 28-year-old's time at Old Trafford is up, and it would be surprising if the Red Devils triggered the extension clause in the defender's current contract.

That being mentioned, the arrival of compatriot Mauricio Pochettino could hand Martinez a second chance this season, with the centre-back potentially playing himself back into favour at the Theatre of Dreams.

  • Returning to action following the final international break of the year, St Mirren make the short journey to Celtic on Saturday looking for a victory that could draw them level on points with the teams in the top half of the Scottish Premiership.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Calum Burrowes | 19 Nov 2026 14:47, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:19.

Returning to action following the final international break of the year, St Mirren make the short journey to Celtic on Saturday looking for a victory that could draw them level on points with the teams in the top half of the Scottish Premiership.

The Bhoys entered the break with a return to winning ways in the league courtesy of a narrow 1-0 victory over bottom-placed Kilmarnock, while the Buddies suffered their second consecutive defeat with a home loss to Rangers.

After securing a record-extending 56th Scottish top-flight title on a dramatic final day of the season in May, Celtic began the 2026-27 campaign hoping for more of the same, retaining Martin O'Neill as manager, and he will take charge of his 339th game at the helm this weekend.

While they currently sit top of the Scottish Premiership with a four-point cushion over arch-rivals Rangers, their season has been far from straightforward, with the Bhoys entering the international break having recorded just one league victory in their previous three outings.

A home draw against Dundee United was followed by a defeat away to Falkirk, their first loss to the Bairns in nearly two decades, before they were presented with an opportunity to return to winning ways against basement side Kilmarnock, although their eventual 1-0 victory was far from convincing.

O'Neill's side took the lead through Republic of Ireland international Liam Scales but were made to work hard for all three points against a team that has won just twice all season.

Celtic have struggled even more in Europe, with just one victory from their opening four Europa League matches leaving them 32nd in the 36-team league phase and facing an uphill battle to reach the knockout stages.

Meanwhile, St Mirren have endured a difficult spell since their 2-1 defeat to Celtic in September, losing seven of their subsequent nine league matches and collecting fewer points than any other side in the division during that period, although their early-season results have at least kept them clear of the bottom two.

Led by Craig McLeish, who took charge on a permanent basis in June, the Buddies have won four, drawn two and lost seven of their opening 13 league fixtures, with the teams below them potentially able to close the gap through games in hand.

While they secured a narrow victory over Dundee in October, St Mirren have collected just one point from their subsequent three top-flight outings, extending their disappointing run of form.

The appointment of a young manager with ambitions of introducing a progressive style of football has yet to produce the desired results, with the Buddies' 12 goals scored representing the joint-lowest total in the division, while their 22 conceded is the second-highest.

After beating Kilmarnock 1-0 in early September, St Mirren sat second in the table with 10 points from a possible 12, but collecting just four more across their next nine matches has brought their promising start to a halt, although that early form provides a platform for McLeish's side to build on if they can rediscover their confidence.

Celtic Scottish Premiership form:.

Celtic form (all competitions):.

St Mirren Scottish Premiership form:.

Unlike their upcoming opponents, Celtic had several players away on international duty over the past fortnight and may need to make changes depending on their fitness following the additional travel.

Auston Trusty recently took a break from football following the death of his father and has not featured for O'Neill's side since their 4-1 Europa League defeat to Benfica in October.

However, he scored for the USA against Haiti during the international break and dedicated his goal to his father, potentially putting himself in contention for a return this weekend.

Alistair Johnston would have travelled to North America to join up with the Canada squad but remains sidelined with a hamstring injury sustained during a 2-1 victory over Hibernian at the end of October.

The Canadian full-back and German midfielder Mika Baur are O'Neill's only expected absentees, although it remains to be seen whether Kasper Hogh will retain his place up front after failing to score for the 16th consecutive match last time out.

As for St Mirren, they could name the same starting XI for a second consecutive match, although McLeish may be tempted to make changes following the two-week break.

Nikolas Agrafiotis, Malik Dijksteel and Keanu Baccus have all been sidelined through injury but are expected to return in the coming weeks, with Saturday potentially coming too soon for some of the trio.

Jonah Ayunga is also unavailable through injury and is not expected to return until early 2027.

Celtic possible starting lineup:.

Johnstone; Donovan, Carter-Vickers, Scales, Tierney; McGregor, Baur; Duran, Nygren, Jota; Hogh.

St Mirren possible starting lineup:.

Chapman; Fraser, Gogic, Jackson; Ramsay, Phillips, Taylor, John; Ramos, Young, Kabia.

The division's highest scorers come up against its least productive attack this weekend, and we expect that gulf in quality to be reflected at Celtic Park.

Celtic should have enough to secure a second consecutive league victory, extending their lead over St Mirren and maintaining at least a four-point cushion over Rangers heading into the following weekend.

By Matthew Cooper | 19 Nov 2026 14:51, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 14:51.

Oxford United will be looking to continue their good form when they welcome Wycombe Wanderers to the Kassam Stadium on Saturday.

The hosts right now sit third in the League One table, while the visitors are 13th.

Oxford are unbeaten in their last 10 league matches, a run that saw them beat local rivals Reading 2-0 in their most recent league game.

That was followed by a disappointing 1-0 defeat to Stevenage in the FA Cup round, but Oxford did bounce back with a 4-0 thrashing of Cheltenham Town in the EFL Trophy.

Aaron Ramsey's side will be looking to carry that momentum into Saturday's fixture, knowing that a win could see them move into the automatic promotion places if results elsewhere go in their favour.

Oxford boast the second best defensive record in the division, having conceded just 11 goals in 13 games, and they have kept three clean sheets in their last four league games.

However, it is worth noting that Oxford have not beaten Wycombe in their last seven meetings across all competitions.

Wycombe travel to Oxford looking to continue their good form, having gone unbeaten in their last five games across all competitions.

Their most recent fixture was a 2-0 victory away against Accrington Stanley in the FA Cup, which saw Connor Taylor open the scoring before Daniel Harvie added a second.

The Chairboys had also recorded a 2-0 League One victory over Burton Albion in their most recent league outing, with Jayden Wareham and Cauley Woodrow on target.

Tom Hounsell will be delighted with his side's improvement in recent weeks and he will be hoping his side can cause an upset against Oxford on Saturday.

Oxford are expected to be without winger Aidomo Emakhu after he was forced off against Cheltenham with an injury and Jin-woo Jeon could replace him.

Mark Harris is set to lead the line, while Cameron Brannagan and Kai Andrews are likely to start in midfield.

Wycombe will be without Danny Ings after the striker picked up a hamstring problem against Accrington and Wareham is set to start up front instead.

Fred Onyedinma and Malik Mothersille are expected to feature out wide, with Josh Scowen and Caolan Boyd-Munce continuing their partnership in midfield.

Oxford United possible starting lineup:.

Cumming; Kioso, Helik, Brown, Currie; Andrews, Brannagan; Jeon, Goodrham, Dembele; Harris.

Wycombe Wanderers possible starting lineup:.

Hazard; Grimmer, Taylor, Hagelskjaer, Harvie; Scowen, Boyd-Munce; Onyedinma, Woodrow, Mothersille; Wareham.

Both sides are are enjoying a good run of form in the league, but Oxford's strong defensive record and home advantage should give them the edge.

Bloodthirsty Brighton feast on rattled Arsenal

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, overpowered and overrun, Arsenal were subjected to the sort of gruelling treatment they usually inflict on their opponents.
  • In the biggest test of their season so far, Arsenal fell woefully short of the standards they have set themselves over the past few campaigns.
  • Brighton were everything that Arsenal are expected to be: aggressive, inventive and dominant across the field.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, overpowered and overrun, Arsenal were subjected to the sort of gruelling treatment they usually inflict on their opponents. Mikel Arteta’s side did not look anything like Premier League champions here, as Brighton and Hove Albion produced a stunning performance full of swarming energy and breathless bravery.

In the biggest test of their season so far, Arsenal fell woefully short of the standards they have set themselves over the past few campaigns. This sort of thing simply does not happen to Arteta’s side. Well, it did not happen. Not before this monstering on the south coast, where the Brighton fans were whipped into a frenzy by the brilliance of Fabian Hürzeler’s players.

Brighton were everything that Arsenal are expected to be: aggressive, inventive and dominant across the field. They even scored with a set-piece, as one of Arsenal’s great strengths became a sudden weakness. Everywhere Arteta looked, the foundational truths of his team were being shaken by a Brighton storm. It was their first defeat by a three-goal margin since May 2023, also against Brighton.

Remarkably, this is now the third consecutive season in which Brighton have beaten the reigning Premier League champions. They are rarely happier than when they are on the hunt against more illustrious opponents, working as a team to snap at heels and then attacking in numbers. They are known as the Seagulls, but they played more like a pack of bloodthirsty wolves. The ferocity of their off-the-ball work, especially in the first half, was extraordinary.

Industry observers note that not for a long time have Arsenal been as rattled as they were here. David Raya misplaced passes, Gabriel Magalhães lost duels and Bruno Guimarães chased the ball in vain. It was Brighton’s Pascal Gross, rather than Arsenal’s Martin Odegaard, who shaped the game in midfield. It was Brighton’s Charalampos Kostoulas, rather than Arsenal’s Kai Havertz, who offered incisive class in attack.

Gross and Kostoulas both struck from range in a one-sided first half, before Chema Andrés added the third after the break. At half-time, Arteta had sprinted down the tunnel towards the dressing room. Whatever messages he gave to his players, they either did not sink in or did not work. By the end, Arsenal were lucky the scoreline was not even more humiliating.

Arteta’s players had come through some tricky assignments in winning their first seven matches of this season, but this was their toughest test yet and they failed it badly. They did not handle the emotions of the occasion particularly well, either: in stoppage time, a frustrated Declan Rice kicked out at Malick Yalcouyé. He was perhaps fortunate to avoid a red card.

In a recent development, it was the first time that Rice and Guimarães had started alongside each other for Arsenal and it swiftly became clear that their £180m partnership will need some work. Arsenal would have hoped their experience in the Premier League would allow for an instant connection but, evidently, that is not the case. Guimarães was hooked after 60 minutes, but might easily have been removed at the break.

According to recent reports, both managers had a similar assessment of the match and how it was won: Brighton did the basics far better than Arsenal. “How we wanted to approach this game was getting into it through small wins,” Hürzeler said. “Everyone speaks about a goal or chance as a win, but a small win can be the first throw-in, the first corner, win the first header, win the first tackle. These small things. If you win these small steps, and celebrate them as a win, then you can gain bigger and bigger wins.”.

It has been revealed that it was typical of Brighton that one of their fresh signings produced an excellent performance in midfield. Andrés, a 21-year-old Spaniard signed from Stuttgart at the end of the transfer window, looks to be the latest gem identified by their data-led recruitment model. No one inside the Amex Stadium was thinking about Carlos Baleba, sold to Manchester United, when Andrés made his tackles and won his headers.

Another upcoming signing, centre-back Luka Vuskovic, was similarly impressive at the back. Signed for £46m from Tottenham Hotspur, Vuskovic looks more than capable of going to the top of the game.

This was perhaps the first occasion this season in which Arsenal missed William Saliba, the injured centre-back who has been so fundamental to their success in recent years. The Frenchman can always be relied on to provide calmness and composure at the back, even under intense pressure. Without him, Arsenal were uncharacteristically jittery.

“The amount of technical errors we did in our own half...” Arteta bemoaned. “We didn’t respect any principle of play that you have to get out of those man-to-man situations. That put us always on the back foot.”.

Recent findings suggest that gross, who at 35 is playing as well as ever, opened the scoring with a low shot from range after 31 minutes. Kostoulas then struck the second, from a similar distance, after some end-to-end action resulted in Arsenal’s midfield and defence melting away. The third was the most simple, as Andrés headed in at the back post from an inswinging corner.

Arsenal did have some chances, with Havertz missing the best of them, but there was never a sense that Brighton were vulnerable. The pressure on the home side was never sustained. For Arteta, who now has an extended international break in which to ruminate on this defeat, it all made for an unfamiliar and unexpected pain.

Mikel Arteta mentioned his Arsenal players failed to “respect the game” as their perfect start to the season was ended in stunning style by a brilliant Brighton performance.

Sources indicate that arsenal’s capitulation on the south coast led to their first defeat of the campaign and Arteta admitted that Brighton had a different “edge” and “bite” throughout the match. The Arsenal manager also said the 3-0 loss represented a “significant lesson” for his players.

“There are certain basics you need to accomplish in football, especially in the Premier League, that we were very far from,” Arteta noted. “From the first throw-in you could sense it, it was so clear.

Recent findings suggest that “It was a really disappointing result and performance. Brighton were another gear up from us. We were extremely poor technically and were not respecting the game.

It has been revealed that “It is not going to take away what the team has done in the last six or seven weeks since coming back from the World Cup. What we have done and the way we have competed, and the amount of games we have won, has been remarkable. But this is a big lesson for all of us to understand what it takes to win at this level.”.

Arteta added that his team did not “respect the principles of play” that were required against Brighton’s intense pressing, and also mentioned his players were guilty of numerous technical errors.

According to recent reports, “Credit to Brighton for what they have done because they have overcome us and they had another edge,” Arteta noted. “There are a lot of moments when the ball is 50/50 and it changes hands and most of the time it was for them.”.

Brighton are the Premier League’s top scorers this season with 16 goals in five matches so far, and this emphatic victory took them up to third place in the table.

Recent findings suggest that “It was a special win,” Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton head coach, noted. “Not only because we played the best team in England but because of the performance. I am really proud of my team. It’s always notable to enjoy these moments. We were horrible to play against. My players really trust each other on the pitch.”.

In a recent development, two things, one give credit to them. In the manner that they played and committed to every single action. We were below the standards that are required for us but in the Premier League as well.

When you miss chances like we did it becomes impossible. I want to congratulate Brighton for what they’ve done. It’s a significant lesson for us to learn. If I have to describe how the team has played and competed in the last six or seven weeks, has been expectational but today has been a big lesson.

A very disappointing result and performance. Full credit to Brighton the manner they went about the game, they were a different gear from us. We didn’t do the basics right for long periods, especially in the first half. We didn’t win enough duels, and any second balls and that stretches you.

We were poor technically when we had the ball in our own half, we didn’t apply the principles that you need against a team that wants to press you man to man.

Arteta: "There are certain basics that you need to accomplish in the Premier League that we were very far from. The amount of technical errors we did... we didn't respect any principle of play. We were always on the back foot. They had another edge.".

Beating the current champions and maybe the best team in England is something special. The result is nice but the performance is what makes it special, the boys showed real courage, real intensity and they were horrible to play against because we did the basics right.

Intensity, intensity, winning the personal duels...we have to have the belief to compete with the best teams in the league. My players really trust each other on the pitch. If one player is out then another can replace him.

Industry observers note that overall we wanted to be really good in every phase. We needed to be at the highest level. We go game by game. After the international break we have a lot of games. After wins like this we have to stay humble and understand why we had this win. We have to keep on going.

Arsenal’s first defeat by a three-goal margin since May 2023.

Just three minutes of stoppage time remaining, but Hull are still pushing bodies forward.

Matt O’Riley has missed two great chances to make it four. Brighton have not given Arsenal a sniff. It will be interesting to hear how stern Arteta is in his post-match assessment.

What a start for Newcastle United and what will really please manager Matthias Jaissle is the way both goals have come from his players winning notable tackles.

A short, intricate pass to Willock inside the box and then a surging, twisting run from the halfway line and the perfectly timed pass to Lewis Hall who stroked a first time shot into the bottom corner.

Hull have been outfought so far which is precisely the response Newcastle’s manager had demanded.

For some of us of a certain age, vertical football just seems like clever new terminology to describe an old idea.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of today’s Premier League 3pm kick-offs, with Brighton vs Arsenal the pick of the three matches.

Industry observers note that brighton are the league’s top goalscorers so far this season and have amassed the most expected goals, but the champions have the league’s best defence and are seeking five wins from five to start their title defence. There is some welcome needle between Fabian Hurzeler and Mikel Arteta, dating back to Declan Rice’s contentious second yellow for delaying the restart two years ago, as well as the Brighton manager’s comments about Arsenal’s style of play in March.

Industry observers note that that 1-0 Arsenal victory at the Amex coincided with Man City dropping points at home to Nottingham Forest on a pivotal night in the title race. Bukayo Saka scored a deflected shot in the ninth minute, and Arsenal held on from there in an ugly but resolute display.

Sources indicate that with Saka, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz fit and firing, as well as the introduction of Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to Arteta’s midfield stable, Arsenal’s football has been more technical and enterprising so far this season. Brighton are one of the few teams who will back themselves to play through Arsenal’s press, which should make for an absorbing game.

Elsewhere, Newcastle are looking to bounce back from their shellacking at Leeds at home to surprise package Hull City. Mattias Jaissle’s team took four points from Liverpool and Spurs but there is concern about how many shots they are conceding. Hull remain unbeaten and continue to confound the odds and underlying data, but that surely cannot last forever.

According to recent reports, everton are also one of the division’s unbeaten teams, but will be targeting three points from a home game against Ipswich after three consecutive draws. Ipswich are sitting comfortably on six points after their win at Crystal Palace, though they did have the extra man for the majority at Selhurst Park.

By Seye Omidiora | 19 Nov 2026 15:09, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 09:25.

Separated by three places in the Premier League table, 12th-placed Tottenham Hotspur welcome Ipswich Town to the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Saturday seeking a return to winning ways on matchday 11.

Leeds United halted Spurs' three-match league winning streak before the hiatus, and the capital club now aim to begin a seemingly favourable run of fixtures with a positive result against the Tractor Boys.

Roberto De Zerbi could have been forgiven for entering the international break disappointed after Leeds ended his side's three-match winning run at the start of the month.

Spurs scored seven goals and conceded just once across victories of 3-1, 2-0 and 2-0 over Coventry City, Chelsea and Crystal Palace to close out October, following a creditable 1-1 draw with 10 men at Manchester United.

Returning to home comforts in the capital presents an ideal opportunity for the Lilywhites to regain winning momentum as they pursue a third consecutive triumph in front of their supporters after victories over Coventry and Palace.

The upcoming schedule will quietly please De Zerbi, whose team face Ipswich, Sunderland, Fulham and Hull across their next five matches, offering encouragement ahead of those encounters with bottom-eight clubs.

Having already collected eight points from a possible 12 against the other four sides in the bottom eight, Spurs, at the moment four points behind fifth-placed Chelsea, will target another victory that could lift them into the division's top half.

Overcoming Ipswich will be far from straightforward for the North Londoners, despite the Tractor Boys winning only one of their last six Premier League matches and losing three.

The defeats suffered by Gary O'Neil's men against Everton, Manchester City and Bournemouth have all been narrow, underlining their battling qualities.

With their other two matches outside a 2-1 home victory over Fulham producing draws against Nottingham Forest (1-1) and Hull City (2-2), the travelling supporters will hope for another competitive showing from the promoted side.

That ambition is tempered by Ipswich collecting just four points from a possible 15 away from home this season, although O'Neil's men have recovered from a 5-2 gameweek two thrashing at Manchester United to beat Palace 3-2 and draw 2-2 at Hull, either side of defeats of 1-0 at Everton and 3-2 at Man City.

Although they have conceded at least twice in four of their five away matches since returning to the significant time, the travelling supporters will back their side to secure a positive result if they deliver another spirited performance outside Portman Road.

Mohammed Kudus has yet to score a league goal this season, but the playmaker's three assists and ability to threaten from unlikely positions make him a potential match-winner for the home side.

No Spurs player has scored more league goals than Jan Paul van Hecke, a notable statistic for the two-goal centre-back ahead of Saturday's encounter with the Tractor Boys.

O'Neil's side, meanwhile, have five players with two goals apiece: Emersonn, Jack Clarke, Julio Enciso, Leif Davis and Zian Flemming.

By Saikat Mandal | 19 Nov 2026 15:30, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:33.

Kilmarnock and Aberdeen face off in an early relegation six-pointer in the Scottish Premiership on Saturday at BBSP Stadium Rugby Park.

Killie are rock bottom in the Scottish Premiership table with nine points from 13 matches, while Aberdeen are just two points and one place above them.

Kilmarnock have shown glimpses of a promising side under Neil McCann, but their reckless defending is proving to be a major stumbling block.

They have managed just two wins in 13 league matches, losing eight of those encounters, and are enduring a particularly difficult spell, having suffered three defeats in their last four outings.

Killie have scored 13 goals this season, showing that they possess the attacking threat to trouble opponents, but their defensive frailties are turning into a recurring nightmare.

McCann's side have conceded 29 goals so far, more than any other team in the division, and unless they address that problem, climbing the table will become an increasingly difficult task.

The East Ayrshire club have won just once in their last seven matches, while their home form has been particularly poor, with only five points collected from six games and 15 goals conceded.

Earlier this week, Aberdeen appointed Mario Frick as their new head coach following the dismissal of Stephen Robinson.

There is an acute sense of instability at the club, with the former Liechtenstein striker becoming their fourth manager in 2026, following Robinson, Peter Leven and Jimmy Thelin.

Frick guided Vaduz to promotion in 2020 before helping Luzern avoid relegation in 2021, and he will need to work similar magic at Aberdeen as the club look to navigate their current crisis.

The Dons have lost four consecutive matches across all competitions and managed just one victory in their last six Scottish Premiership outings.

Aberdeen have collected only four points on the road this season, but they have lost just once to Kilmarnock in their last six meetings across all competitions.

McCann does not have any major injury concerns, with goalkeeper Maksymilian Stryjek his only absentee.

The 30-year-old is currently sidelined with a knee injury but is expected to return by the start of next month.

It will take time for Frick to get a better understanding of his squad, but his immediate priority will be to motivate the players and prevent another defeat in this crucial encounter.

The Dons, meanwhile, are without Lewis Mayo (foot), Chris Cadden (hamstring), Kristers Towers (knee), Emmanuel Gyamfi (thigh) and Mats Knoester (tendon), although all five are expected to return by the middle of next month.

A newly introduced manager often brings fresh energy to a team, and that could provide Aberdeen with the much-needed impetus to avoid a fifth consecutive defeat. The Dons are unbeaten in their last three meetings with Killie, and we back them to preserve that record in this crucial encounter.
